comment: The public roadmap. `bun nv site --check roadmap` keeps it in step with the goal chain, and `bun nv site --roadmap` copies it into README.md. `internal` lists the goals that are not public work.

themes.title: Clearer method names
themes.text: Every method that changes something has a verb in its name. Every method that returns `bool` reads as a question, such as `isEmpty`. A method that returns a changed copy says so, such as `resized`. The changelog lists each old name and its new name.

themes.title: Documentation links
themes.text: A `@see` tag can name a file in your project, and a heading in a Markdown file. The editor follows the link, and `nvs pkg pack` checks that the package contains the file.

themes.title: Faster reflection
themes.text: `Core\Reflect` builds the description of each class once, so reading it again costs nothing. `PropertyInfo` tells you if a property is `lateinit` or `readonly`.

themes.title: Dates and times
themes.text: `==` compares two dates, times or durations by their value. `Date` gets methods for the start and end of a period, the difference between two dates and a range of days. `Duration` reads and writes clock text such as `01:30:00`.

themes.title: Dates and optional values in routes
themes.text: A query parameter with the default `null` is optional. Dates and times can be route parameters and query values, and `Core\Router::url` writes them as ISO text. Dates, times, durations and UUIDs are written to JSON as text.

themes.title: Extending classes you do not own
themes.text: An `extend` block adds methods, constants and properties to a class from `Core` or from a package. A file sees the added methods when it imports the block with `use`.

themes.title: Callbacks for the calling class
themes.text: A parameter of type `callable(static)` takes a function for the class that the call names. The compiler checks each call of that function.

themes.title: Enums as keys
themes.text: A `match` over an enum must cover every case or have a `default`. Constants can contain enum cases. `array<E, T>` is an array whose keys are the cases of the enum `E`. The editor adds the missing `match` arms for you.
